canal_p03_001.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_001.text: The buyer's agent stood on the private wharf before the morning fog lifted. He wore boots clean enough to make the workers stare and carried a list longer than the loading crane's arm. Han read it beside him with his mouth set hard. The list named platforms, hooks, store chests and the crane itself as security for the conditional deposit. It did not name the common canal bed. Yue could see how a narrower lawful claim might still unsettle everyone who worked beside the disputed water.

canal_p03_002.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_002.text: Luo asked the agent to keep the public path open while he counted gear. He said the inventory would take only an hour. Bao pointed to a stacked cargo frame blocking the marked rope corridor and asked which hour included the grain boat's scheduled turn. The agent disliked the question but moved the frame with two workers. A private inspection could proceed without stopping the whole canal. The first concession came through a pair of ordinary hands lifting wood, not a declaration of principle.

canal_p03_003.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_003.text: Han introduced the agent as his buyer's appointed receiver, with authority to inspect the pledged loading gear. The deposit agreement allowed recovery if the claimed sale title failed, not immediate seizure merely because the review was pending. An Ru had not yet arrived, but the clerk could read that line. The receiver agreed to inventory without removal. Han looked relieved and ashamed in the same instant. His threat had become a postponed practical possibility rather than disappearing through the council's sympathy.

canal_p03_004.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_004.text: Bao examined the crane support from the dry outer side while its beam stayed unloaded and secured. The lower pin had worn its socket oval. A full swing under the largest old cargo portion might shift the foot toward the common path. Han's worker had reduced portions after feeling the change. The receiver wanted the original capacity recorded as a sale value. Bao would record the posted historical rating and the current restriction separately, refusing to price a damaged machine as if its best year still lived inside it.

canal_p03_005.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_005.text: The wharf worker who had lent his socks to the child admitted he had not written the reduced portions down. He feared Han would accuse him of slowing trade. Han began to object, then remembered yesterday's extra hauling pay and closed his mouth. Luo asked the worker to demonstrate the current safe stop from the ordinary control. He did, with the beam unloaded. The machine halted cleanly. They had learned one working function and one worn structural limit, both necessary to its actual description.

canal_p03_006.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_006.text: Tian arrived with the worker's repaired gloves and found the receiver counting them among the wharf tools. She snatched the gloves from his board. They belonged to the worker, bought from his wages, not to Han's pledged gear. The receiver corrected the entry after the man confirmed ownership. Tian kept watching his pen. A broad inventory could swallow personal objects as easily as the auction notice had swallowed time. This time the mistake was corrected while the owner stood close enough to answer.

canal_p03_007.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_007.text: The receiver said small disputed items should not delay a large business. Pei Fen, seated near the office door, asked whether he would mind lending his boots to the total. He did not smile. Han did, unexpectedly, and the workers laughed before remembering they were worried. The receiver crossed out the gloves and marked personal items excluded. Pei had changed the room with a joke that made the boundary visible. Yue helped move her chair out of the lifting lane before the laughter distracted anyone from the secured crane.

canal_p03_008.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_008.text: The old chest sat beneath Han's desk, its lock stained green around the plate. Pei recognized the repair stitch in one bundle when Han opened it, but the specific toll-book reference appeared in another. Her remembered blue thread had led close, not exactly. Yue copied the bundle labels without declaring the first memory false in every detail. The household work record could be inspected when An Ru arrived. Han closed unrelated contracts beneath a plain board and left the requested bundle ready in the office.

canal_p03_009.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_009.text: The receiver wanted the chest included as a movable asset, without its documents. Han asked him to defer that line until the archive comparison finished. The receiver agreed to value the empty chest now and leave custody unchanged through the review. Bao measured its damaged foot and said it needed repair before being carried. Pei protested that everyone had become more interested in the chest's wood than its contents. Yue said the contents would be easier to preserve if the bottom did not fall out on the path.

canal_p03_010.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_010.text: Beyond the office, Tian's newly repaired sail billowed from a boat preparing to leave. Its owner paid the last ordinary stitching amount at the counter. She counted it in front of Yue and said this was what an honest completed bargain looked like: thread, work, a usable sail and money that arrived. Yue teased her for making a speech about a handful of copper. Tian admitted she wanted to practice before speaking to Han without shouting. The practice did not prevent her from pocketing the coins with visible relief.

canal_p03_011.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_011.text: Luo checked the public path's width beside the private shed. The shed wall stood inside its plot, but a rain gutter drained directly across the paving. In dry weather it left only a dark strip. During a heavy shower it could turn the towline station slick. Han had meant to extend the gutter and never found a convenient week. Bao proposed a small ordinary channel under the paving with an access cover. It would require agreement where private runoff crossed common maintenance space.

canal_p03_012.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_012.text: Yue crouched near the gutter and found old soap residue caught behind a paving edge. The wharf workers washed loading cloth there. She nearly called the residue evidence of deliberate obstruction, then remembered the household song mistake. It showed a use of water and a likely source of slippery film. The work practice could change without assigning intent from a pale mark. Luo asked the workers where their rinse went and had the contained washing place moved away from the live path.

canal_p03_013.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_013.text: Han's buyer arrived in person before noon, irritated that the suspended notice had acquired more qualifications. He asked whether the canal would still be navigable by auction day. Luo answered that necessary repairs had their own schedule and authority. The buyer wanted a yes; the keeper could offer current conditions and named work. Han watched the exchange with the strange satisfaction of a man seeing someone else denied the confident answer he had been requesting for three days.

canal_p03_014.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_014.text: The buyer had planned to store grain on the seasonal spill hollow. Bao laid the old flood plan beside the boundary survey and asked where that lost volume would go. The buyer suggested raising the far bank. Luo said the far bank protected households below the fork, who had not been asked. A proposed commercial improvement might send its cost downstream. Yue marked those households for a later site visit, adding people the first auction map had made nearly invisible.

canal_p03_015.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_015.text: Tian asked the buyer whether he expected to own her work after the review. He said he expected whatever service the valid contract actually conveyed. The answer was narrower than the notice she had read. Han admitted the notice's successor list exceeded his surviving transcription's annual total. He had not yet accepted that the pledge ended entirely. Tian wanted to hear the larger concession first, but Yue saw that the smaller one would also matter if the original annex took longer to find.

canal_p03_016.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_016.text: The buyer reduced his provisional offer because the claimed labor value and spill storage were uncertain. Han gripped the table's edge. He had built his private repayment plan on an amount that might never arrive. The receiver said the deposit's loading-gear security remained enough for a narrower recovery. Wharf workers looked toward the crane, their actual livelihood. The public review had removed an inflated value from the sale without producing wages for people caught beneath the resulting arithmetic.

canal_p03_017.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_017.text: Yue went outside before she said something unhelpful. Tian followed and asked whether she pitied Han. Yue said she pitied the workers and understood his fear, which was not quite the same thing. Tian accused her of splitting feelings into safe little boxes. Yue answered that anger had not told them whether a crane belonged to the public. They both stopped. A boat horn sounded from the bend, and neither had the excuse of pretending the argument mattered more than the keeper's next passage.

canal_p03_018.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_018.text: Luo let the boat through while the buyer waited behind the red board. His receiver stepped forward to hurry him and caught a rope loop around one boot. Han's worker pulled him back before the line tightened. The man looked offended until he saw the live pull reach the place where he had stood. He thanked the worker quietly. For the next passage, he waited at the actual marked boundary. The wharf had instructed him through an avoided injury his long inventory list could not predict.

canal_p03_019.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_019.text: The gate timber arrived in a two-piece cart load, one expected length and one shorter reserve plank. Bao checked the delivery against the invoice before unloading. The second full replacement length was still delayed, exactly as the supplier had warned. Han's buyer offered to buy the shorter plank for the wharf. Bao said it belonged to the public work order's specified reserve stock. A fair buyer could request a purchase; the carpenter could decline without turning the request into an attempted theft.

canal_p03_020.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_020.text: Yue helped carry the reserve plank to the keeper's dry store. Its ordinary weight pulled her shoulder when she reached around a post. She stopped, changed sides with the other carrier and finished the turn without qi. The work took longer and annoyed the waiting cart driver. Luo told him the delay was a handling problem, not a second fee. Yue could accept that modest public embarrassment more readily after correcting a larger one at yesterday's meeting.

canal_p03_021.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_021.text: Pei found an old loading label beneath the delivered cart's reed mat. It named the founding flood's timber cutter, whose successor had supplied today's replacement length. The name gave them a living route to purchase copies older than the public register. Han recognized it as well and offered the cutter's last known address. He had been defending his mother's loan through household names. A supplier's real delivery record could help establish the debt without treating those households as the material she bought.

canal_p03_022.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_022.text: The clerk wrote separate requests for the cutter's timber account and the toll-book work entry. Tian wanted to send one broad demand for every old record. An Ru's arriving letter recommended narrower references so keepers would know which actual bundles to search. Yue helped address the envelopes. The private cutter's books might corroborate paid material. The toll book might corroborate completed labor. Combining them too soon would hide the difference between a debt balance and a work obligation, exactly the mistake the notice had exploited.

canal_p03_023.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_023.text: At the wharf, Bao began a temporary ordinary brace for the crane's worn support. It would permit only the reduced current load after testing, while a full repair waited for Han's private order. The brace came from Han's own timber stock. Yue helped mark its placement from outside the secured beam's arc. Han watched the work, then asked whether the public gate crew could simply fit the new pin too. Bao referred him to a separate quote. Their common repair allowance did not cover his crane by convenience.

canal_p03_024.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_024.text: Han disliked the separate quote but accepted it after his worker explained the lost loading turns. Tian helped the man compare the proposed working interval with his shift. They could clear cargo before the brace went in, then resume smaller portions. The buyer's receiver asked to observe the test because it would affect the gear's value. Bao agreed. An opponent's observation could strengthen a sound test if he stood where the actual safety plan allowed him, rather than where his authority made him want to stand.

canal_p03_025.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_025.text: The brace test exposed another weakness: the outer platform board sagged beneath the secured sand load. Bao stopped before the crane swung. Han had replaced that board's visible top while leaving an old split bearer below it. The wharf worker knew it creaked but thought the carpenter had inspected everything. Bao had never seen the underside until today. Yue wrote the inspection's actual extent on the work note. A repair could be real and still leave a hidden support outside the work that was ordered.

canal_p03_026.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_026.text: Han sat on a coil of rope while Bao revised the private repair. His clean coat had collected sawdust, mud and a long wet mark near the knee. He asked Yue whether the canal council would delay the auction if he admitted the title failed. She could not promise its legal decision. She could say the review date remained eight weeks and his cash claim would be examined separately. He looked toward the workers, then asked what she would do with the deposit if she were him.

canal_p03_027.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_027.text: Yue said she would first stop counting a sale price that had not become available money. Han laughed without amusement. She had no private wharf, no inherited loan and no creditor at her door. That was true. She asked him to explain the deadline and assets he actually had, rather than accept her sentence as advice. He named the gear, two late customer payments and a small reserve for wages. The practical list made the fear less theatrical and more difficult.

canal_p03_028.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_028.text: An Ru stepped from the afternoon mail boat carrying one small satchel. Pei stood too quickly to greet her, then remembered the clinician's instruction and sat again. The archivist looked at the wharf, the secured crane and the waiting household packet before asking for tea. She would compare the books after hearing how the documents had moved. Yue had expected her arrival to produce an answer. Instead it produced a better first question, and the receiver groaned at another careful beginning.

canal_p03_029.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_029.text: The afternoon now held three separate jobs. The private crane needed its brace and underside inspected; the old chest needed its requested pages compared without exposing unrelated contracts; the wharf workers needed a clear account of how inventory restrictions would change their next wages and shifts. Luo would oversee public access while Bao, An Ru and Tian led those tasks. Yue could take one position with them, carrying enough knowledge to help and enough uncertainty to ask when the work changed.

choices.text: Inspect the private crane supports with Bao.
Compare the offered toll-book pages with An Ru.
Help Tian clarify the private workers' wages and shifts.

canal_p03_030.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_030.text: Bao led Yue beneath the platform only after the beam was secured and the lower work area cleared. Two workers watched the ordinary supports from above. The space smelled of old river mud and cedar dust, with daylight entering through gaps between boards. Yue could see the split bearer without crawling below its weight. Bao reached it with a long probe from the supported side. Its surface broke into pale dry crumbs, unlike the sound timber beside it.

canal_p03_031.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_031.text: The receiver leaned over the edge to demand a closer look. Bao told him to remain above and lowered the probe with a crumb still attached. Yue held a white board behind it so he could see the fracture. The man admitted the damage affected his valuation. Han asked whether the bearer could be patched cheaply. Bao said the ordinary crane load needed a continuous supported path, not a beautiful outer strip nailed across a failed middle.

canal_p03_032.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_032.text: They traced the bearer's ends and found one seated on a stone belonging to the old public bank wall. The private platform had used that wall as support through an agreement Luo's predecessor made for one season. The written renewal had never been located. Han had maintained the platform for years and assumed continued use meant approval. Bao could repair its private timber, but the shared support required a separate decision. The structure had made the title questions physically inseparable without making them identical.

canal_p03_033.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_033.text: Yue asked whether removing the platform would weaken the public wall. Bao checked the contact and found the wall supported the platform, rather than relying on it to stay upright. That mattered to a possible removal plan. It did not mean the platform could be dropped into the water without consequences. They would need unloaded sections carried onto the private plot, with the path closed for a named interval. Han listened more carefully once the plan treated his property as something that could survive the dispute.

canal_p03_034.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_034.text: The worker who controlled the crane had a folded glove beneath his belt. Its worn thumb showed where the ordinary release rubbed during every smaller cargo swing. Tian's repair had thickened the wrong side for that grip. He had not wanted to complain after her help. Yue sent for her, and she recut the patch while the inspection continued. A useful gift could need adjustment without becoming an insult. The worker tested the changed glove on an unloaded handle and smiled for the first time that day.

canal_p03_035.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_035.text: Bao's revised private repair used a new bearer from Han's sound stock and a support foot entirely within the loading plot. It would leave the public wall unloaded by the platform. The new position reduced the crane's safe swing by a narrow angle. Han objected because one favored boat position would become inconvenient. Luo marked an alternative berth inside his private frontage. The choice preserved the gear and public support, while making his loading operation slower in a way he would actually notice.

canal_p03_036.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_036.text: Yue helped mark the crane's revised arc on the deck with washable chalk. The receiver wanted the mark made permanent before accepting it. Bao said the unloaded geometry trial would precede a durable sign, because a wrong permanent line would simply become a confident mistake. They swung the secured empty beam under its ordinary control and checked the clearances. It passed the inner store corner but stopped short of the public path. The smaller useful movement looked disappointingly modest from a distance.

canal_p03_037.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_037.text: Han tested the new cargo position with an empty boat and found his favored platform ladder in the way. He kicked the ladder's foot, then immediately checked whether anybody stood below. Nobody did. His worker moved it to the other side. Yue saw the apology begin in Han's face before he said it aloud. The bank dispute had pressed on every small inconvenience in his business. He could still decide how to treat a worker standing inside that pressure.

canal_p03_038.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_038.text: When the private repair quote was complete, Han accepted the reduced swing and separate support. The payment would come from his loading account, with the public work order unchanged. Bao scheduled the actual fitting after the gate's ordinary guide task so the same carpenter was not promised in two places at once. Yue brought the revised geometry to the clerk. The private wharf could continue trading under limits, buying Han time without validating the canal sale.

canal_p03_039.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_039.text: At the office door, An Ru waited with the requested work packet. The household record showed a fourth-season reference the original annex search could follow. Tian had checked the workers' actual upcoming shifts, and no inventory list had acquired their gloves or wages. Yue added Bao's support map to the shared findings. The three jobs had narrowed a large frightening threat into particular goods, particular work and particular documents. Han still owed a deposit answer; the canal still needed its leaking gate repaired.

canal_p03_040.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_040.text: An Ru asked Yue to begin with how the household receipt left its blanket. The seamstress had cut cloth, the clerk had dried the original and an earlier copy had arrived from a tea tin. Yue described the actual sequence she knew and identified the others who could confirm the handling. The archivist wrote no dramatic heading. She used the receipt's reference number, then asked Han to open only the matching toll-book bundle beneath the board covering his other contracts.

canal_p03_041.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_041.text: The matching page recorded work in the pledge's fourth season, including two later replacement days added after the first twelve-day acknowledgment. Its entry referred to a sick household by a clear exterior number. The wet receipt's fourteen and the earlier copy's twelve now fit a dated sequence. An Ru kept all three versions. The older copy had not been false; it had been earlier. Tian looked relieved when Yue explained that distinction to her, as if a family memory had been allowed to remain complicated without becoming worthless.

canal_p03_042.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_042.text: Han's transcription omitted the annex heading because its copy began midway down a page. A note on the back instructed a past clerk to attach the preceding leaf before filing. That leaf was absent from his working bundle. Han had followed the visible text without its duration line. An Ru recorded the incomplete copy and asked for the register containing the preceding leaf. A real omission could explain his belief. It did not preserve the notice's enlarged annual total after the omission was known.

canal_p03_043.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_043.text: Pei remembered sending the original register to the valley archive during a toll-house roof repair. The current public index listed the transfer but no completed return. An Ru compared its number with her own receiving copy and found a storage reference in a neighboring bundle. The register had not vanished into an abstract ancient past. It had moved along an ordinary recorded path and then been filed where nobody looking only at the canal cabinet would find it.

canal_p03_044.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_044.text: Yue asked whether the private chest could now be released from the search. An Ru said the offered toll page had been copied and witnessed, while the unrelated contracts remained covered. Han could keep his papers even if the empty chest later passed under the deposit agreement. The receiver accepted that and corrected his custody note. The review had obtained useful public evidence without taking every private transaction as a trophy. Han watched An Ru's pen with a cautious gratitude he did not offer to Yue.

canal_p03_045.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_045.text: Pei wanted to accompany the archive journey. Her eyesight would make the damaged pages tiring, and the clinician had advised against a full travel day immediately after the dizzy spell. An Ru proposed taking Pei's indexed recollection and returning a legible extract for her comparison. Pei disliked the substitute until the archivist promised to preserve disagreement rather than force her memory to match the found text. Yue carried the broad notebook to the copying desk while Pei dictated the search details.

canal_p03_046.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_046.text: The buyer examined the matched work entry and asked whether fourth season meant final season. An Ru pointed to the missing annex heading. The toll page established which season and how many days; it did not establish the pledge's whole duration. Yue had made exactly that overclaim yesterday. She gave the narrower answer before the archivist needed to correct her. Han noticed. He still distrusted her public certainty, but she had begun supplying a reason to trust her corrections.

canal_p03_047.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_047.text: The original loan receipts matched Han's stated repayment of one hundred sixty against the two hundred forty advanced. An Ru would compare the original terms before certifying the remaining eighty's security and collection method. She said that clearly enough for Tian to hear. The household advocate frowned but nodded. A valid monetary claim might survive the collapse of the labor and title claims. The review could change what Han could take without pretending his family had supplied timber for nothing.

canal_p03_048.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_048.text: Han offered Yue tea while An Ru finished the references. The cup contained ginger, which made her think of Wei Xiu's explicit dislike and smile unexpectedly. Han thought she was mocking the bargain and stiffened. Yue explained the harmless memory. He laughed, embarrassed by his assumption. An awkward conversation recovered through a small specific truth. For a moment they were simply two tired people near a kettle, each trying not to let the day's arguments describe every sound the other made.

canal_p03_049.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_049.text: At the office door, Bao brought the revised private crane-support map and Tian brought the workers' shift notes. The requested toll page had been copied, the incomplete annex heading identified and the original register located for tomorrow's archive journey. Yue added the receipt sequence to the shared findings. Their work would not settle everything today. It had made tomorrow's search precise enough that the missing seasons could finally become a document question rather than an endless argument about gratitude.

canal_p03_050.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_050.text: Tian began with the wharf's next wage day rather than its auction value. Five workers expected payment at week's end. Han showed the amount reserved for their completed shifts and agreed to keep it outside the receiver's gear inventory. The deposit security named movable equipment, not money already earned by labor. The receiver checked that wording and entered the distinction. Yue watched the workers' shoulders lower. A future dispute over jobs had become slightly less frightening when today's earned pay stopped drifting toward it.

canal_p03_051.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_051.text: One worker wanted to leave before the crane repair and asked whether he would lose the two mornings already worked. Han said no, then asked for notice to arrange a replacement. Tian wrote the completed work separately from future availability. The man planned to help his sister harvest reeds and might return afterward. The private business needed a usable schedule. It did not own the gap between his departure and possible return merely because he had worked there yesterday.

canal_p03_052.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_052.text: The oldest worker wanted to stay even if the crane's reduced swing slowed his cargo handling. He knew the boats, their owners and the old berth's ordinary currents. Tian had expected every worker to prefer the common crew if the sale failed. Yue asked him what staying would require. He named a repaired support, accurate cargo portions and wages on the actual date. Those requests were neither loyalty surrendered nor loyalty purchased. They were conditions under which a familiar job could remain worth doing.

canal_p03_053.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_053.text: A young worker asked whether joining the public gate crew would make him liable for the old household pledge. His parents rented inland and had never belonged to the towpath list. Tian showed the posted paid task rather than the successor register. Its workdays were new employment, not payment of inherited debt. He wanted one morning moving guide timber. Bao would assess the ordinary handling crew before confirming it. The man left with a real application and no new family obligation.

canal_p03_054.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_054.text: Han's receiver asked to count the personal loading hooks because workers used them on his platforms. The workers produced purchase notes and one plainly handmade hook with its owner's initials. Shared use did not make those objects Han's security. Tian recorded the offered evidence without copying unrelated wage purchases. The receiver corrected the inventory again. He had arrived with a list of apparently simple goods. The actual wharf kept supplying owners more specific than the place where an object happened to be lying.

canal_p03_055.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_055.text: Tian's anger eased while the oldest worker described teaching Han to pole a boat as a boy. He remembered the merchant falling into shallow water and insisting he had meant to swim. Han looked horrified that the story had entered a serious inventory meeting. The worker told it anyway, then asked for the crane pin to be replaced before another generation learned the wrong kind of courage there. Yue laughed with them and noticed that the request sounded firmer after the affection made it personal.

canal_p03_056.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_056.text: They agreed on a temporary shift plan during the private repair: smaller portions, one loading station at a time and a defined pause while Bao fitted the support. Han would pay the extra scheduled handling interval from his own account. The public gate job would not absorb those private wages. Tian asked the clerk to keep the two rosters separate because the same worker might serve both. The resulting board looked untidy, with arrows and crossings. Everyone on it could still point to their actual next task.

canal_p03_057.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_057.text: The worker who had nearly seen the receiver caught in a live loop offered to teach him the ordinary waiting position. The receiver declined proudly, then accepted when the buyer asked how long another inventory would take. Yue watched him practice standing behind the board during an unloaded demonstration. The wharf's work was not mysterious. It required attention to a line that could tighten suddenly, and the willingness to let somebody with less expensive boots tell him where to put them.

canal_p03_058.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_058.text: Tian asked Yue to read the shift agreement aloud because she distrusted her own temper after yesterday's argument. Yue stumbled over one worker's name and let him correct her before continuing. Han signed the completed-wage separation and future private repair shifts. Nobody signed for the worker who had chosen the reed harvest. The wharf now had a temporary workable plan while its ownership and deposit questions continued. The agreement gave people something to do besides waiting beside a frightening list.

canal_p03_059.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_059.text: At the office door, Bao brought the private support map and An Ru brought the matched household work sequence. The incomplete annex heading had led to a surviving archive register. Yue added Tian's wage and shift notes to the shared findings. Today's inventory could proceed without swallowing personal hooks or earned pay. The public path stayed open between cargo turns. Tomorrow's search would examine what the original four seasons meant, with workers able to leave this evening knowing how Friday would actually be paid.

canal_p03_060.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_060.text: The shared findings went onto three boards because the office table was too small. Bao's private support plan hung beside An Ru's receipt sequence; Tian's shift note stayed near the door where workers could read it before leaving. The receiver checked his corrected inventory against them. Han still disputed the canal title, but he could no longer describe the entire wharf as one undifferentiated possession. His own goods, workers' tools and public support had acquired separate names that changed what could happen next.

canal_p03_061.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_061.text: The crane remained secured until its private bearer repair and test. Han paid the workers for the already agreed waiting interval, then released them with tomorrow's revised start. He disliked paying for a machine that stood still. The oldest worker said stillness was cheaper than a fallen load. Han looked at the worn socket and accepted the comparison. Yue heard no grand reconciliation. She heard an employer choosing one practical cost rather than letting the next cost arrive as an injury.

canal_p03_062.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_062.text: Pei stayed after everyone else left the office. She admitted she had once copied the household names onto a maintenance rota without writing its end date at the top. Another clerk later attached that rota to Han's transcription. She had meant to help schedule willing workers, not create a permanent successor list. Tian listened with her jaw tight. Pei did not ask her to make the admission comfortable. She asked the clerk to preserve it as one part of the copying history, with the actual original still to be compared.

canal_p03_063.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_063.text: Tian said she was tired of discovering that nobody intended the thing that kept happening to her family. Pei answered that intention would not restore the missing heading, and she would help find it. Yue had expected an apology to make the room gentle. It made the anger more specific instead. Tian could speak to the woman who once held the pen, rather than argue with a vanished administrative fog. She agreed to compare Pei's recollection after the archive extract returned.

canal_p03_064.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_064.text: Han's wife brought supper to the closed wharf and found him staring at the inventory. She asked whether his mother's loan had always included the canal itself. He said the original toll share might prove otherwise. She put the bowl down beside him and asked what he would do if it did. Yue heard only that much from the public path. The question belonged to their household. She passed without stopping to collect a private conversation merely because its answer would interest the review.

canal_p03_065.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_065.text: The conditional deposit was forty-eight copper. Han would owe its return if the offered title failed under the agreement, with the listed loading gear securing the amount. His unpaid public loan balance was eighty, a different transaction with a different debtor. Yue wrote the two sums on separate pages when the clerk explained the available terms. Han had begun acting as if one hoped-for sale would solve both. The coming original comparison might remove that hope before it removed any actual obligation.

canal_p03_066.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_066.text: At the keeper's bench, Jiang showed Yue the prepared relay's copper path beneath a translucent ceramic cover. A fine green trace followed its intended route when the enclosed test source was admitted, stopping at the ordinary trip. The light made the worn gate's dimensions briefly resemble a living drawing. Yue wanted to touch it. Jiang handed her the unpowered comparison tile instead. Its smooth cold surface carried the same shape without the glow, and she could examine it while the live apparatus remained guarded.

canal_p03_067.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_067.text: Jiang closed the test supply and asked Yue to explain which part of the beautiful trace actually moved the gate. Yue pointed to the prepared command lead and the separately powered actuator, then admitted the illustration made the whole machine feel smaller than its physical load. Jiang liked that answer. She would rather have an apprentice notice the drawing's seduction than memorize an assurance. Outside, Bao's real timber remained too long to carry through the shed door without turning it.

canal_p03_068.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_068.text: Tian arrived with two bowls and found Yue still examining the cold tile. She asked whether cultivating made the world more vivid. Yue said sometimes it made one small sensation so vivid she forgot the room around it. Tian held a thread against the lamp and said good stitching did something similar. They ate without deciding which skill was grander. Yue's desire for more routes remained, but it had acquired company: another person could care just as fiercely about a seam most people never noticed.

canal_p03_069.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_069.text: An Ru planned the archive journey for morning. The public transfer entry named the original register's destination; her receiving index gave a likely storage shelf. Yue would accompany her for the comparison and return with approved extracts. The canal originals staying at the wharf remained with their actual owners. Luo adjusted Yue's scheduled ordinary workday to the archive task, keeping the gate crew covered. A useful search should not quietly remove the apprentice from a job somebody else expected her to perform.

canal_p03_070.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_070.text: Bao inspected the arriving full timber length again before signing its receipt. A dark patch near the end proved to be surface staining over sound wood within the usable section. He marked it and kept the supplier's grade note beside the measurement. Han's rejected shorter cedar remained his own stock. Yue liked watching the two men discuss wood without forcing their larger disagreement into every grain line. The gate would use a piece chosen for the actual span it had to carry.

canal_p03_071.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_071.text: Luo checked the temporary public-path arrangements through a full boat turn. The private wharf's reduced work had sent walkers along the high yard longer than planned, and one grain-house owner wanted his normal access restored before dawn. Bao could finish the brace fitting before the first morning cargo, then reopen the ordinary path after inspection. The owner accepted that deadline and kept the jars inside one more night. A modest agreement held because its inconvenience had a visible end.

canal_p03_072.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_072.text: The receiver returned the workers' personal hooks to their marked places after completing his own witnessed inventory sketch. Yue noticed he had drawn the crane's old swing rather than the reduced arc Bao had just tested. She asked him to compare the chalk line. He corrected the drawing with a second ink, leaving the earlier arc visible. The buyer would receive both with an explanation, rather than a neat private picture that silently restored the unsafe capacity.

canal_p03_073.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_073.text: Pei prepared a large-script letter for the archive. She described the transfer during the roof repair, her remembered annex heading and the clerk whose rota had later been attached. Yue read it aloud for her before folding. The retired woman corrected a surname and made one sentence less certain. She had begun treating remembered detail as something worth preserving carefully, rather than something weakened by admitting its limits. Tian took a copy home and said she would read it after finishing tonight's sail.

canal_p03_074.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_074.text: The eldest wharf worker met Han at the door with his completed shift tally. Han checked it and confirmed Friday's payment before asking whether the man wanted another week under the repaired crane's restrictions. He agreed, if the support passed its actual test. Han said yes. Yue could hear the condition without a lecture attached. The canal had not acquired the worker. The private wharf had not acquired him either. Tomorrow they would have to keep offering work worth his continued choice.

canal_p03_075.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_075.text: A gull landed on the secured crane beam and seemed to enjoy the position more than anybody had enjoyed the machinery that day. Bao threw a small piece of reed past it, failing to move the bird. Tian whistled with the child's repaired instrument and sent it flapping toward the spill hollow. Han complained that she had become the keeper of all troublesome creatures. She replied that the most troublesome one had washed his own boot. He laughed before remembering to look offended.

canal_p03_076.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_076.text: At dusk, the private brace fitting ended without cargo movement. Bao checked its fasteners and left the crane secured for the daylight reduced-load test. The receiver accepted a current restriction on his valuation note. The public bank wall remained unloaded by the new support position. Luo signed only that shared-wall finding, leaving the private machine's approval to Bao's separate inspection. The work had changed tomorrow's possibilities through real wood and real limits, while the canal title still waited in an older book.

canal_p03_077.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_077.text: Yue packed for the archive with the clerk's request, Pei's offered recollection and her own work notebook. She left the project tile and relay supplies at the keeper's shed. The journey would not be an escape from difficult people; she would return to Tian's anger, Han's deposit and Luo's leaking gate. She found that prospect reassuring. A document could answer one question while leaving her responsible for how she spoke to the people whose lives the answer changed.

canal_p03_078.speaker: narrator
canal_p03_078.text: The mail boat waited under a pale morning sky. An Ru took the forward seat and put the packet where ordinary spray could not reach it. Luo checked the towline guide before their departure, then waved them toward the archive road. Behind them, the private wharf prepared its restricted test and the public gate crew measured the first timber. Ahead lay the original register's four seasons, if the receiving index still led where it claimed. Yue sat with her hands quiet and watched the canal narrow into the river.
